name: themeguard
description: Audits a project's CSS colour variables: value collisions between roles, dead tokens, ramps that collapse between themes, and families a theme tunes everywhere except the members it silently inherits.

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build

//:
0.1.0 is the first release with something to run: `themeguard <file.css>` audits a stylesheet from a terminal, and the library is importable via the exports map. The tarball ships dist/ only — src/ and tests/ (including the 96 KB vendored calibration fixture) are development assets and stay out of it. 0.1.1 adds the optional themeguard.config.json, discovered beside the stylesheet, for marking specific findings deliberate. 0.1.2 lets an entry scope what it suppresses: a `tokens` set the finding must carry in full (a deliberate pair as ONE entry), and a `theme` narrowing the entry to findings measured in that theme — printed as [theme: …] / [tokens: …] on the suppressed line. 0.1.3 says WHERE: collision, scale-collapse and family-consistency findings now carry `sites` — the declaration each measured token resolved from — and end their message with it (`Declared at lines 41 and 33.`), citing the cascade winner rather than every place the name is written; dead-token, which already named `:root:402`, is unchanged. 0.1.4 adds the site-scoped half of suppression: a `/* themeguard-ignore <rule> [--token …] -- <why> */` comment in the stylesheet itself — trailing on the judged declaration or standalone on the line above — suppresses only findings living at its site, so a refactored defect re-reports instead of being held down by a judgement recorded elsewhere, and the report's suppressed section prints the directive's `[file:line]` source clause. 0.1.5 adds the report's `unmatched (N)` section — the complement of `suppressed`: every declared suppression that matched NOTHING, named with its rule, scope, source and reason, printed even at zero, never moving the exit code — so a judgement that has outlived its defect (or never aimed at one) can announce that instead of going silent. 0.1.6 adds the fifth rule, `unresolved-reference`: a `var()` naming a custom property that NO scope declares — a typo'd use, a fallback pointing at nothing, a declaration built on a name nobody wrote, or a `@theme inline` alias chain into a typo — which today passes green while the property falls back to unset/inherit or to the written fallback. One predicate over the references the parser already collects: one finding per name with every use site listed, `@theme inline` declarations count as declaring, suppression entries and themeguard-ignore directives target it through the same rule-id door, and it moves the exit code like any finding. 0.1.7 takes one invocation over several stylesheets: `themeguard a.css b.css` audits each file independently — the config beside each governs it, references do not cross files — and aggregates the per-file outcomes into one exit with the precedence 2 > 1 > 0, fail-fast on the first file that cannot be audited, so a CI or pre-commit caller gets one invocation and one verdict. 0.1.9 adds the sixth rule, `cycle-reference`: a `var()` loop — per CSS custom-property semantics every property in the loop, and every `var()` consuming a member, is invalid at computed-value time, yet the shape audits green because `dead-token` sees both names referenced and `unresolved-reference` sees both declared. One finding per (loop set, author) over the resolver's existing `kind:"cycle"` chains — no parse or resolve change: a loop authored outside any theme's own block (the base `:root` declarations, or the `@theme inline` alias namespace) is one `theme: null` finding, a loop a theme's own declarations close is a theme-scoped finding, and a theme that merely inherits a root-authored loop never re-reports it; the message names the loop as written, cites the cascade-winner declaration lines, and states the consequence. 0.1.11 lets a config judgement name the stylesheet it was recorded against: an optional `file` on a suppression entry, relative to the config's own directory and strictly validated (absolute, empty or non-string exits 2 naming the entry), resolved by the CLI before matching — a file-scoped entry governs that one stylesheet, so a directory sharing one config among sibling stylesheets can record a judgement for tokens.css without it silencing buttons.css; an entry without the field is byte-identical to 0.1.7, and an unmatched file-scoped entry now prints ` [file: …]` and a carve-out in the unmatched prose: for it, the report CAN tell — the judgement aims at the sibling the clause names, and that file's report states its fate. 0.1.10 makes the audit unit the file's IMPORT CLOSURE instead of one file: the parser collects the `@import` statements in CSS-legal position and a new `loadStylesheet(entry)` loader follows the RELATIVE ones (`./`, `../`, quoted or `url()` form, media suffix ignored) against the containing file's directory — bare package specifiers, absolute paths and missing targets are skipped silently (import-resolution failures are not findings), cycles terminate on the visited file, and imported scopes/references splice in statement order BEFORE the importing file's own, each carrying an additive `origin`. The rules' predicates are untouched — that is the fix: lookups now hit imported declarations, killing the false unresolved-reference/dead-token defects each file of an import-composed pair reported about the other. Sites read from an imported file cite it (`declared at tokens.css:2`) — in every rule's message, the `Declared at …` clause included, since two sites of one finding can now sit in two files and each is cited independently (`Declared at tokens.css:3 and line 7.`); root-file sites render byte-identically. The resolver folds the merged scopes in DOCUMENT order, not per-file line numbers — line numbers restart at 1 in every imported file, and a line sort handed the cascade to whichever theme block sat deeper in its own file, reporting collapses that no browser sees and passing over real ones — so an importing file's own re-declaration of an imported theme token wins exactly as the cascade says. Site-scoped themeguard-ignore directives stay entry-file-only and match entry-file sites only: a directive never silences a finding spliced in from an imported file whose line merely coincides. `resolveCss` stays the text-only library entry (no base directory known, no imports followed), and the CLI's config doctrine is unchanged — themeguard.config.json sits beside each ROOT stylesheet and governs the whole closure of the file it sits beside: an unscoped entry matches by rule/token/theme alone, and a file-scoped entry (0.1.11) names the entry stylesheet itself, so either spelling covers the closure's imported files. 0.1.12 adds the seventh rule, `duplicate-declaration`: a custom property declared more than once in ONE scope with differing values — the cascade keeps the last declaration and silently discards the rest, so the file the author reads says one thing and the browser paints another, and until this rule the shape audited green while coverage even deduped it into one token. The rule reads the pre-fold declarations the way dead-token walks scopes (no parse or resolve change), skips only the @theme inline reference layer — never alias names, since duplicate-ness is judgeable from the source — reports one finding per source block with the shadowed and winning sites and both values named (deduped across the two scope halves a selector-list prelude yields), never reports a cross-scope override (the theme system working) or a same-value repeat (harmless copy-paste), and moves the exit code like any finding. 0.1.13 makes config discovery walk UP: themeguard.config.json is found at the stylesheet's directory first, then each ancestor, bounded at the filesystem root — nearest wins (the eslint/tsconfig prior), so a ledger at styles/ governs styles/components/ too, and every pre-0.1.13 beside-the-stylesheet layout is byte-identical (its config is the walk's first hop). A file scope resolves against the config's DISCOVERED directory (was: always the audited stylesheet's), making the schema's documented "relative to the config's own directory" true in general rather than by coincidence of layout; a scope naming a file outside the config's directory-and-below can never be honoured, and the unmatched section says so. 0.1.14 adds the eighth rule, `unresolved-import`: a RELATIVE `@import` edge the loader could not follow — the file the specifier names is missing or unreadable. The failure was swallowed in a bare `catch { continue; }`, so a stylesheet whose own composition could not load audited green (`@import "./toens.css";` with a one-character path typo printed `No findings.` and exited 0). The loader now records every failed relative edge on the sheet it returns (`Stylesheet.unresolvedImports`, classified `missing`/`unreadable`, accumulated across all frames so an edge broken two hops in is named with its own from-file) and the rule emits one finding per entry — specifier as written, the resolution outcome, the consequence (the file never loads, so every declaration inside it is invisible to this audit) and the statement's own position, cited by file for a non-entry frame. Cycles and shared repeats stay unrecorded (the visited set dedupes them browser-style), and bare package specifiers, absolute paths and URLs keep v1's silence byte-identically. The vendored calibration fixture's own broken edge (`@import "./actiontext.css"`) is resolved by a comment-only stub, so the 22-finding census keeps its numbers and its bytes. 0.1.15 adds the ninth rule, `theme-partial-token`: resolution is per-theme, but rule 5 asks a stylesheet-wide question, so a token declared only in ONE theme's block was unjudged everywhere else. The rule reads the resolver's per-theme `kind:"unresolved"` fact directly and partitions it against rule 5's population — a missing reference declared in NO scope stays rule 5's (a typo is one defect, never reported twice); one declared SOMEWHERE but absent from the view that breaks on it is this rule's. One finding per missing NAME (never per consumer or per theme), `theme: null` like dead-token, naming the declaring theme(s) with their declaration sites (imported declarations cited by file, like every rule's), the unresolved view(s) and the consuming chain(s); it moves the exit code like any finding, and is suppressible through both doors with no directives change. The direct-consumption face (a component rule's var(), no declaration chain) is a recorded residual, deliberately out of v1: telling correct theme-scoped CSS from a defect needs selector-prefix reasoning the parser does not do. 0.1.17 gives the pipeline caller the DATA beside the number: `--json`, the command's first and only option, replaces the prose on stdout with NDJSON — one compact object per stylesheet, the AuditReport verbatim with the audited path in front of it, key order following the report object's own insertion order. The exit codes do not move (the flag adds a channel, it does not relocate the verdict), diagnostics stay prose on stderr in both modes so stdout is never mixed, and fail-fast leaves the lines already written parseable. The flag is position-free and idempotent; `themeguard --json` with no stylesheet stays the usage error it has always been. 0.1.19 lets an in-source judgement travel with its file through composition: /* themeguard-ignore … */ directives are scanned from EVERY member of the audit's import closure, each imported file's entries stamped with its entry-relative origin, so a vendored file's judgement is honoured wherever the closure that imports it is audited — matched on (origin, line), never on a bare line across an edge — and a malformed directive in any member exits 2 naming its own file and line. 0.1.20 completes the resolver's coverage of its own CYCLE fact: a `var()` loop whose closing edge is EMBEDDED in a compound value — `--divider: 1px solid var(--divider-color)` closed by `--divider-color: var(--divider)`, or the `calc(var(--pad, 0px) + 2px)` self-increment idiom — minted no `kind: "cycle"` token at all, because the walk followed a `var()` only when it was the ENTIRE value, so `cycle-reference` (whose whole subject is that fact) was structurally silent on the commonest shape real CSS writes token values in and the coverage inventory listed both loop members as healthy. Where the whole-value branch declines, the compound value's PRIMARY-position `var()` references are now read for a back edge onto a name already on the walk, and one found mints the identical fact the whole-value path mints; a reference inside a `var()`'s own FALLBACK segment is never an edge (the walk's existing semantics — the primary name is the edge, a fallback is descended into only when the primary is undeclared — applied to compound values rather than changed), so `--a: var(--b, var(--a))` keeps its full `--a → --b → --a` chain. Every whole-value shape is handled above the scan and is byte-identical by construction, a compound value with no back edge falls through unchanged, and every rule file is untouched — the rule's input became complete and the rule did not move. 0.1.21 completes the resolver's dependent-declaration half: a token whose walk STOPS at a compound value is re-marked kind:"cycle" when the stopped value's primary-position references name a walk-minted cycle in the same theme view, so a tail into a compound loop (`--card-border: var(--divider)` where `--divider: 1px solid var(--divider-color); --divider-color: var(--divider)`) and a compound tail into a whole-value loop carry the designed finding the whole-value shapes always carried — the consult reads the walks' finished results only (per theme, primary-position edges, never a compound value chased), the re-marked chain carries the stopping walk plus the loop it depends on so loop-set grouping emits it as its own finding beside the loop's, a healed loop member joins its own group as a rotation (finding counts unchanged), and a compound value referencing another compound-stopped value two hops from the loop stays a pinned residual. 0.1.22 makes that dependent-declaration consult COMPLETE in the two directions 0.1.21 left open: it asks loop MEMBERSHIP — is the referenced name inside a var() loop in this theme's view, read from the token table so an undeclared chain name is never a member — instead of the walker's kind-carrying identity, which made a byte-identical tail fire or stay silent according to which member of a compound-closed loop its walk happened to close; and it iterates to a FIXED POINT over its own re-marks (bounded by the theme's candidate count, each round reading a snapshot taken at its start so the outcome is order-independent), so a dependent two or more hops from the loop — 0.1.21's pinned residual — resolves, and one consumed through a whole-value walk stops vanishing from the report. Healthy compound chains that never reach a loop keep their literal classification, whole-value shapes stay byte-identical by construction, every rule file is untouched, and the one remaining residual — a loop whose EVERY member stops at a compound value mints nothing to propagate from, a gap in MINTING rather than in completing — is pinned. 0.1.23 mints that missing loop: a names-only cycle pass over the theme's PRIMARY-position edges — declared names only, fallback segments unread, no value substituted, an edge naming nothing declared a dead end — runs per theme view before the dependent-declaration pass, finds the loops no walk closes (an all-compound loop, or any loop whose members stop every walk short of the circuit), and marks their unmarked members `kind:"cycle"` with the loop chain spelled from themselves, so rule 6 groups and emits them exactly as it does every other loop; a walk-minted chain is never rewritten (every pre-existing loop shape stays byte-identical), a dependent that enters such a loop completes on the existing fixed point with no further change, and the calibration fixture's graph — 140 primary-position references, none cyclic — mints nothing, keeping its 22-finding report byte for byte. 0.1.24 makes the `unmatched` section's advice true for the arm where both its readings were false: an entry-file `themeguard-ignore` directive whose rule and tokens match a collision living in an IMPORTED member of the closure suppresses nothing — correctly, the fence is unchanged — and the report then told its author the defect was fixed or the entry never aimed at anything real, while the finding printed three lines above and the judgement was ONE FILE MOVE from working, with nothing naming where. The row now names the live finding and its `file:line` and the two moves that reach it (move the comment into that file, or record the judgement in the config, whose reach is the closure), the section states the third case beside its two readings, and `--json` carries the same pointer as an additive `crossFileAim` key on the unmatched row (absent, never null, on every row without one). Derived from the matcher's OWN halves rather than a twin that could drift — `matchesEntryIdentity`, `findingLinesIn` and `findingSiteCoordinates` hoisted out of `audit()` and exported, matching semantics byte-identical — and claimed only where the FILE is the whole reason nothing matched (no site of the finding lives in the directive's own file at all): a directive that missed on its LINE while its own file holds a site keeps the existing advice, whose clauses are closer to true there, and so does an entry matching nothing, and so does every config entry, whose identity matching is already closure-wide. DIAGNOSIS, never suppression: no matching-semantics change, the entry stays on the leg, the counts and every exit code are byte-identical, no CLI flag and no config schema change.
; 0.1.25 splits the skipped row's reason on the skip branch's own arms: one condition (from===undefined || to===undefined || kind!=="color") already distinguished three whys and reported all three as not-a-color, two of them falsely — a pair declared only in a sibling theme's block has no value in this view to be a colour or not, so the row asserted something about a value the view does not have, and a var() chain that found nothing is exactly what the unresolved-reference section says about the same token three sections down, so one report diagnosed one token two contradictory ways — the reason is now read at that condition's own || boundaries into absent / unresolvable / not-a-color, and an absent row names the sibling theme the pair actually lives in with each member's line, cited through the same list positionClause is now a frame around rather than a second spelling of it; translucent and not-a-color keep their exact strings and populations, the widened union reaches --json additively as new reason values plus an absent-never-null declaredIn key, and no count, no finding and no exit code moves; 0.1.26 makes the unmatched section's advice true for the last arm where both its readings were false — a config entry whose theme scope names one of the five rules that report theme: null by construction (dead-token, duplicate-declaration, theme-partial-token, unresolved-import, unresolved-reference, each pushing the literal at its own push site because what it measures is a fact about the stylesheet rather than about one theme's view of it) can never match anything, in this file, any file of the closure or any run of that config, and was told the defect was fixed or it never aimed at anything real while the finding printed above and the judgement was one KEY DELETION from working: the row now names the rule, the dead scope and the move, the section gains its own tellable-case line beside the two it had, --json carries the same diagnosis as an additive themelessAim key absent on every row that did not earn it, and the rule's theme-lessness is DECLARED beside the rule ids rather than inferred from one run's findings, so cycle-reference's conditional themeAuthored ? theme : null stance keeps the generic prose even in a run whose loops all happen to be base-authored, and an entry that also carries a file scope keeps it too — the theme not being the only reason nothing matched there; the matching semantics, the counts and the exit code do not move.
